<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#topGrad)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="1200" height="50" fill="#0D1117"/>
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="5" height="50" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="58" y="43" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">China alone accounts for ~31% of global CO₂ — more than the US and EU combined</text>

  <!-- Page title -->
  <text x="40" y="90" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">China Now Emits More Than One-Quarter of Global CO₂</text>

  <!-- ====== TREEMAP ====== -->
  <!-- Treemap area: x=40, y=105, w=830, h=530 -->
  <!-- Total area = 830*530 = 439,900 px² for 100% -->
  <!-- China: 31% → 136,369 px²; US: 13%; India: 8%; EU27: 6%; Russia: 5%; Africa: 3.5%; SAm: 3.5%; Int'l: 3%; Other: 26% -->

  <!-- China block (largest): x=40, y=105, w=450, h=303 (~31%) -->
  <rect x="40" y="105" width="450" height="303" fill="#1E40AF" rx="4"/>
  <text x="265" y="230" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="36" font-weight="bold">China</text>
  <text x="265" y="272" text-anchor="middle" fill="#93C5FD" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">~31%</text>
  <text x="265" y="298" text-anchor="middle" fill="#BFDBFE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13">of global CO₂ | Rising (slowing)</text>

  <!-- USA block: x=490, y=105, w=250, h=217 (~13%) -->
  <rect x="490" y="105" width="250" height="217" fill="#7C3AED" rx="4"/>
  <text x="615" y="196" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">United States</text>
  <text x="615" y="224" text-anchor="middle" fill="#DDD6FE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold">~13%</text>
  <text x="615" y="246" text-anchor="middle" fill="#EDE9FE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">Declining</text>

  <!-- India block: x=740, y=105, w=130, h=248 (~8%) -->
  <rect x="740" y="105" width="130" height="248" fill="#F97316" rx="4"/>
  <text x="805" y="218" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">India</text>
  <text x="805" y="242" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FED7AA" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">~8%</text>
  <text x="805" y="260" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFEDD5" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Rising</text>

  <!-- EU-27 block: x=870, y=105, w=200, h=134 (~6%) -->
  <rect x="870" y="105" width="200" height="134" fill="#0891B2" rx="4"/>
  <text x="970" y="162" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">EU-27</text>
  <text x="970" y="184" text-anchor="middle" fill="#BAE6FD" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">~6%</text>
  <text x="970" y="202" text-anchor="middle" fill="#E0F2FE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Declining</text>

  <!-- Russia block: x=870, y=239, w=100, h=114 (~5%) -->
  <rect x="870" y="239" width="100" height="114" fill="#6B7280" rx="4"/>
  <text x="920" y="291" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">Russia</text>
  <text x="920" y="310" text-anchor="middle" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">~5%</text>

  <!-- Int'l aviation+shipping: x=970, y=239, w=100, h=114 (~3%) -->
  <rect x="970" y="239" width="100" height="114" fill="#374151" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1020" y="283" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10" font-weight="bold">Int’l Avn</text>
  <text x="1020" y="298" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">+Shipping</text>
  <text x="1020" y="315" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D1D5DB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">~3%</text>

  <!-- Africa block: x=490, y=322, w=125, h=117 (~3.5%) -->
  <rect x="490" y="322" width="125" height="117" fill="#10B981" rx="4"/>
  <text x="552" y="376" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Africa</text>
  <text x="552" y="398" text-anchor="middle" fill="#A7F3D0" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">~3–4%</text>

  <!-- South America: x=615, y=322, w=125, h=117 (~3.5%) -->
  <rect x="615" y="322" width="125" height="117" fill="#14B8A6" rx="4"/>
  <text x="677" y="368" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">South</text>
  <text x="677" y="385" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">America</text>
  <text x="677" y="406" text-anchor="middle" fill="#CCFBF1" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">~3–4%</text>

  <!-- Other: x=740, y=353, w=340, h=86 (~other) -->
  <rect x="740" y="353" width="340" height="86" fill="#E5E7EB" rx="4"/>
  <text x="910" y="400" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Other Countries</text>
  <text x="910" y="422" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">~26%</text>

  <!-- Bottom row label for China extension -->
  <rect x="40" y="408" width="450" height="97" fill="#1E3A8A" rx="4"/>
  <text x="265" y="460" text-anchor="middle" fill="#BFDBFE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13">China’s emissions: ~31% of global total</text>
  <text x="265" y="482" text-anchor="middle" fill="#93C5FD" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">US + EU combined: ~19% — less than China alone</text>
  <text x="265" y="500" text-anchor="middle" fill="#BFDBFE" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">Africa (~3–4%) ≈ Int’l aviation & shipping (~3%)</text>

  <!-- RIGHT ANNOTATION COLUMN (x=1080, w=160) -->
  <rect x="1080" y="105" width="160" height="430" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="6"/>
  <text x="1160" y="128" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">2024 Trends</text>
  <line x1="1090" y1="135" x2="1230" y2="135" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- Trend items -->
  <rect x="1090" y="142" width="140" height="48" fill="#DBEAFE" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1160" y="162" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">China ~31%</text>
  <text x="1160" y="178" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Rising but slowing</text>

  <rect x="1090" y="198" width="140" height="48" fill="#EDE9FE" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1160" y="218" text-anchor="middle" fill="#7C3AED" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">US ~13%</text>
  <text x="1160" y="234" text-anchor="middle" fill="#7C3AED" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Declining trend</text>

  <rect x="1090" y="254" width="140" height="48" fill="#FED7AA" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1160" y="274" text-anchor="middle" fill="#C2410C" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">India ~8%</text>
  <text x="1160" y="290" text-anchor="middle" fill="#C2410C" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Rapidly rising</text>

  <rect x="1090" y="310" width="140" height="48" fill="#CFFAFE" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1160" y="330" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0891B2" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">EU-27 ~6%</text>
  <text x="1160" y="346" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0891B2" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Declining trend</text>

  <rect x="1090" y="366" width="140" height="48" fill="#F3F4F6" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1160" y="386" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">Russia ~5%</text>
  <text x="1160" y="402" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Roughly stable</text>

  <rect x="1090" y="422" width="140" height="48" fill="#D1FAE5" rx="4"/>
  <text x="1160" y="442" text-anchor="middle" fill="#065F46" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">Africa ~3–4%</text>
  <text x="1160" y="458" text-anchor="middle" fill="#065F46" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Slowly rising</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="660" x2="1240" y2="660" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="690" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 via Our World in Data (Ritchie & Roser) | Approx. 2024 shares</text>
  <text x="640" y="690" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="10">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="690" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">4 / 9</text>
</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
  <!-- Dark background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0D1117"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#topGrad)"/>

  <!-- Grid decoration background -->
  <line x1="200" y1="100" x2="200" y2="660" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="400" y1="100" x2="400" y2="660" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="600" y1="100" x2="600" y2="660" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="800" y1="100" x2="800" y2="660" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="1000" y1="100" x2="1000" y2="660" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="1200" y1="100" x2="1200" y2="660" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="60" y1="200" x2="1220" y2="200" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="60" y1="360" x2="1220" y2="360" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>
  <line x1="60" y1="520" x2="1220" y2="520" stroke="#1E40AF" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.1"/>

  <!-- Page heading -->
  <text x="640" y="55" text-anchor="middle" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" letter-spacing="1">Key Takeaways: Responsibility Is Shared but Unequal</text>
  <line x1="300" y1="68" x2="980" y2="68" stroke="url(#topGrad)" stroke-width="2"/>

  <!-- ===== FIVE TAKEAWAY CARDS in 2-column grid ===== -->
  <!-- Card dimensions: w=565, h=140; gap=30 -->
  <!-- Row 1: y=85 (cards 1 and 2) -->
  <!-- Row 2: y=245 (cards 3 and 4) -->
  <!-- Card 5 centered: y=405 -->

  <!-- Card 1: No peak yet -->
  <rect x="40" y="85" width="565" height="140" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="85" width="5" height="140" fill="#D4AF37" rx="2"/>
  <text x="60" y="115" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">01  No peak yet</text>
  <text x="60" y="138" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Global CO₂ from fossil fuels & industry exceeds 35 Bt/yr.</text>
  <text x="60" y="156" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Growth has slowed but emissions have not peaked —</text>
  <text x="60" y="174" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">up from 6 Bt in 1950 and 22 Bt in 1990.</text>
  <text x="60" y="196" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">→ The long-run trajectory remains upward.</text>

  <!-- Card 2: China vs per capita -->
  <rect x="635" y="85" width="605" height="140" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="635" y="85" width="5" height="140" fill="#6366F1" rx="2"/>
  <text x="655" y="115" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">02  China dominates total, not per capita</text>
  <text x="655" y="138" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">China emits ~31% of global CO₂ (largest single share).</text>
  <text x="655" y="156" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Yet per capita: ~9 t — below the US (~14 t) by ~35%.</text>
  <text x="655" y="174" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">India emits ~8% total but only ~2 t per capita.</text>
  <text x="655" y="196" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">→ Total vs. per capita tell very different stories.</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Historical responsibility -->
  <rect x="40" y="245" width="565" height="140" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="40" y="245" width="5" height="140" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
  <text x="60" y="275" fill="#EF4444" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">03  Historical responsibility: Europe & the US</text>
  <text x="60" y="298" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Europe and the US emitted >90% of global CO₂ before 1900.</text>
  <text x="60" y="316" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Still >85% in 1950. Today: under one-third combined.</text>
  <text x="60" y="334" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Cumulative historical stocks drive most current warming.</text>
  <text x="60" y="356" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">→ Historical emissions shape climate justice arguments.</text>

  <!-- Card 4: 150x gap -->
  <rect x="635" y="245" width="605" height="140" fill="#1F2937" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="635" y="245" width="5" height="140" fill="#F97316" rx="2"/>
  <text x="655" y="275" fill="#F97316" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">04  150× per capita gap persists</text>
  <text x="655" y="298" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Chad & Niger: ~0.1 t/person/yr. US & Canada: ~14 t/person.</text>
  <text x="655" y="316" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">The average American emits in <2 days what a person in</text>
  <text x="655" y="334" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Mali emits in an entire year.</text>
  <text x="655" y="356" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">→ Per capita inequality is a central climate justice issue.</text>

  <!-- Card 5: Energy policy (centered) -->
  <rect x="337" y="405" width="606" height="140" fill="#1E3A8A" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="337" y="405" width="5" height="140" fill="#D4AF37" rx="2"/>
  <text x="357" y="435" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">05  Energy policy can decouple prosperity from emissions</text>
  <text x="357" y="458" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">France and the UK achieve similar living standards to the US</text>
  <text x="357" y="476" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">but emit 3–4× less per capita — due to nuclear & renewables.</text>
  <text x="357" y="494" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">Technology and policy choices, not just wealth, determine</text>
  <text x="357" y="512" fill="#E5E7EB" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12">a country’s carbon footprint.</text>
  <text x="357" y="534" fill="#93C5FD" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">→ The path to net zero requires both ambition and the right energy mix.</text>

  <!-- Bottom divider and footer -->
  <line x1="60" y1="568" x2="1220" y2="568" stroke="#1F2937" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="640" y="600" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">Data: Global Carbon Budget 2025, Our World in Data | Authors: Hannah Ritchie & Max Roser</text>
  <text x="640" y="640" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">CONFIDENTIAL · April 2026</text>
  <text x="640" y="680" text-anchor="middle" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11">9 / 9</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

[Transition] Welcome. Over the next fifteen minutes, we'll walk through the most important facts about global CO₂ emissions — who emits, how much, and how that's changed.

This presentation draws exclusively on data from the Global Carbon Budget 2025, published by Our World in Data. The scope is fossil fuels and industry from 1750 to 2024 — the clearest picture we have of where emissions stand today.

Key points: (1) Scope: fossil fuels & industry, 1750–2024 (2) Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 / Our World in Data (3) Audience: policy analysts, negotiators, and sustainability researchers
Duration: 0.5 minutes

---

# 02_global_growth

[Transition] Let's start with the long view — how we got here.

Before industrialization, CO₂ emissions were effectively negligible. [Pause] By 1950, the world was emitting roughly 6 billion tonnes per year. By 1990, that figure had more than tripled to over 20 billion tonnes. Today, we exceed 35 billion tonnes annually.

[Scan Room] This matters because every year without a peak adds to the cumulative stock of CO₂ in the atmosphere — and it's the cumulative stock, not the annual flow, that drives temperature change.

Key points: (1) 6 Bt in 1950 → 22 Bt in 1990 → >35 Bt in 2024 (2) Growth slowing but no peak reached (3) Fossil fuels dominate; land-use change declining slightly
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_regional_shift

[Transition] The total is striking, but the distribution of responsibility has shifted dramatically.

In 1900, Europe and the United States together accounted for over 90% of global CO₂ emissions. [Pause] That's an extraordinary concentration. By 1950, they still held over 85% of the total.

[Data] Today, Europe and North America together account for less than one-third of global emissions. [Benchmark] Meanwhile, Asia — led by China — now produces roughly half. This is a near-complete reversal in less than 125 years.

[Scan Room] The strategic implication is significant for any negotiation: the countries bearing the greatest historical responsibility for the cumulative stock of atmospheric CO₂ are no longer the largest annual emitters.

Key points: (1) Europe+US: >90% in 1900, <33% today (2) Asia: ~5% in 1900, ~50% today (3) Historical vs. current responsibility diverge sharply
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_china_dominates

[Transition] Zooming into today's landscape — one country stands apart.

China now emits approximately 31% of global CO₂ from fossil fuels and industry. [Pause] That is more than the United States (~13%) and the EU-27 (~6%) combined.

[Data] India has emerged as the third-largest emitter at ~8%, and its emissions are rising rapidly. Russia accounts for ~5%. [Benchmark] The concentration at the top is striking: three entities — China, the US, and India — together account for over half of global emissions.

[Scan Room] For negotiators, this concentration creates both urgency and leverage — any meaningful global climate agreement must engage these three actors.

Key points: (1) China ~31%, US ~13%, India ~8%, EU-27 ~6% (2) Africa ~3–4% ≈ International aviation+shipping (3) Top three emitters >52% of global total
Duration: 2 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip Africa/shipping comparison and go directly to per capita]

---

# 05_per_capita_gap

[Transition] Total emissions tell one story. Per capita emissions tell a very different and deeply unequal one.

When we adjust for population, the distribution becomes stark. The United States and Canada emit approximately 14 tonnes per person per year. [Pause] Chad and Niger emit approximately 0.1 tonnes per person. That is a 150-times difference.

[Transition] Let's look at the same countries in more detail — because the per capita framing reframes the China story entirely.

[Transition] This brings us to perhaps the most actionable insight in this entire dataset: energy mix explains most of the difference between comparable wealthy nations.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_annual_change_2024

The picture is mixed. Many Western nations — including the United States, the European Union, and the United Kingdom — saw their emissions decline.
